name: Porsche Carrera GT 5.7 L V10 (type 980/01, 2003-2006)
summary: A 68-degree V10 derived from a Le Mans prototype engine. Because the bank angle is 68 rather than 72 degrees, firing alternates between 68 and 76 degrees: nearly even, with a slight irregularity under the 8,400 rpm shriek.

bore_mm.note: Also en.wikipedia Porsche V10 engine page. Nikasil-coated bores.

rod_length_mm.note: Not found. Rods are titanium (autozine, kfz-tech, en.wikipedia). supercarnostalgia says both 'hydroformed steel conrods' and 'forged titanium connecting rods' in one sentence, which is self-contradictory.

firing_order.note: Not found on any page opened, nor the cylinder numbering.

crank.value: Two connecting rods per crank pin (shared pins, no split), with different firing intervals for the two rods on a pin.
crank.note: kfz-tech: 'the different ignition intervals at each two connecting rods on a crank pin'. Pin spacing is not printed; 68/76 alternation implies five shared pins 72 degrees apart in firing sequence (my inference).

firing_intervals_deg.note: Autozine (enthusiast technical site): 'Its firing was uneven, alternating between 68 and 76 deg'. Consistent with a 68-degree bank and shared pins; 68+76 = 144 = 720/5. No Porsche document found stating it.

valves_per_cylinder.note: DOHC per bank, chain driven, bucket tappets; VarioCam variable timing on the intake cams only; sodium-cooled exhaust valves (de.wikipedia, en.wikipedia).

intake_duration_deg.note: Not found. Porsche normally publishes timing at 1 mm lift, but I could not open a Carrera GT technical data page.

redline_rpm.note: Excellence magazine spec table 'Max RPM 8400'; same figure on en.wikipedia and autozine.

intake_type.value: fixed-length intake with individual inlet funnels (trumpets); no variable intake manifold
intake_type.note: Autozine: 'no such things like variable intake manifolds or exhaust'; kfz-tech mentions the inlet funnels. Throttle arrangement not found.

exhaust_notes.value: Fixed exhaust, no variable flap, per Autozine.

missing: exhaust manifold layout and pipe sizes

sources.what: Porsche Newsroom article (28 Sep 2025) with a technical data table for the Carrera GT. Manufacturer.
Excellence magazine (Porsche specialist) spec table: bore, stroke, max rpm.
Autozine technical review of the Carrera GT; single-author enthusiast site, source of the 68/76 firing statement.
kfz-tech.de (German automotive engineering teaching site) note on the Carrera GT V10: shared crank pins with unequal intervals.
English Wikipedia Porsche V10 engine page; bore, stroke, redline.
German Wikipedia Carrera GT page; valvetrain description.
Supercar Nostalgia guide; noted only for its contradictory rod-material sentence.

name.note: Porsche heritage release, "Technical Data: Porsche Carrera GT", built 2003-2006; the only car with this engine.

curb_kg.note: Quote: "Kerb weight 1,380 kg". ADAC (https://www.adac.de/rund-ums-fahrzeug/autokatalog/marken-modelle/porsche/carrera-gt/980/996732/): "Leergewicht (EU) 1455 kg", which is 1,380 + 75 kg, so 1,380 is most likely DIN (inference).

gear_count.note: Quote: "6-speed manual gearbox with ceramic clutch".

gears.note: Read by a helper, not re-read by veh-d. Quote: "I. 3,20 II. 1,87 III. 1,36 IV. 1,07 V. 0,90 VI. 0,75". carspecs.us (https://www.carspecs.us/cars/2005/porsche/carrera-gt/61583) agrees: "First Gear Ratio 3.20 ... Sixth Gear Ratio 0.75".

final_drive.note: Quote: "Achsantrieb 4,44:1"; carspecs.us agrees ("Final Drive Axle Ratio 4.44"). Check (ours): 4.44 x 0.75 on this tyre gives about 8,400 rpm at 330 km/h.

tyre.note: Rear. Quote: "265/35 ZR 19 / 335/30 ZR 20". Excellence (https://www.excellence-mag.com/resources/specs/259) and carspecs.us agree. ADAC lists 315/35 R20 rear, an outlier.

wheel_radius_m.note: Estimated (ours): rolling radius taken as 98% of the unloaded radius computed from the tyre size (rim diameter / 2 + section width x aspect ratio).

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Porsche Carrera GT' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: rear mid-engine, rear-wheel drive.
